 Print this Article 
 View Comments Mitchell Robinson has started at center in each of the Celtics first three games. Danielle Parhizkaran/Globe Staff After rolling to a 134-99 win over the Bulls Monday night, the Celtics will be right back at it when they host the Nets in the second night of a back to back. 
 The Celtics could have a dramatically different starting lineup. Jayson Tatum (on the floor for 27:41), Paul George (25:08), and Mitchell Robinson (16:07) all suited up on Monday. All three could have rest days because of injury history. 
 “I think it’s twofold,” said Celtics coach Joe Mazzulla. “We trust the sports science team that we have. We trust the competition of those guys. At the same time, I think our locker room has been built on one through 15, 16 or 17 being able to impact winning. So it’s just a combination of all those things. 
 “At the end of the day, we have to do what gives us the best chance to win, and at the same time keep those guys healthy and validate the whole locker room by putting guys in situations where they’ve got to win games for us.” 
 Get Court Sense Keep up with everything Celtics with news, commentary, and analysis from the Globe's all-star team. Arrives twice weekly. Enter Email Sign Up The Nets are coming off a 136-109 beating at the hand of the Pacers on Sunday that dropped them to 0-3. 
 Here is a preview. 
 When: Tuesday, 7:30 p.m. 
 Where: TD Garden, Boston 
 TV: NBCSB. Radio: WROR-FM (105.7). 
 Line: Boston -11.5. O/U: 221.5. 
 NETS 
 Season record: 0-3. vs. spread: 1-2. Over/under: 2-1 
 Last 10 games: 2-8. vs. spread: 3-7. Over/under: 6-4 
 CELTICS 
 Season record: 2-1. vs. spread: 2-1. Over/under: 1-1, 1 push 
 Last 10 games: 5-5. vs. spread: 4-6. Over/under: 3-6, 1 push 
 TEAM STATISTICS 
 Points per game: Brooklyn 111.0, Boston 118.0 
 Points allowed per game: Brooklyn 123.7, Boston 107.7 
 Field goal percentage: Brooklyn .417, Boston .470 
 Opponent field goal percentage: Brooklyn .506, Boston .432 
 3-point percentage: Brooklyn .378, Boston .424 
 Opponent 3-point percentage: Brooklyn .403, Boston .347 
 Stat of the day: The Celtics went 8-5 in the second leg of back-to-back games last season. 
 Notes: The Celtics have beaten the Nets in 11 of the last 12 meetings. … Payton Pritchard had a team-high 28 points in Monday’s win. … Hugo González scored a season-high 13 points in 24 minutes with five rebounds … Tatum is averaging a team-high 24 points. … The Nets led Sunday’s game, 51-49 with 2:45 left in the first half, but Pacers closed the half on a 16-5 run and scored 37 points in the third quarter. … The Celtics will be off on Wednesday and Thursday before welcoming the Bulls back to the Garden on Friday.
